data.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with CIA, but warns: be discreet
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday called for Cubans to make "discreet" contact with the American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island's communist government.

data.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
data.description: GENEVA (SWITZERLAND) - The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said.

data.title: Tottenham Hotspur finally end long wait for a win
data.description: There was a huge sigh of relief at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Monday night when Spurs notched their first league win of the season after seven games. Their 3-1 victory over Coventry City lifted them off the bottom of the table to a slightly more comfortable 16th place.

data.title: Hot Buriram braced for derby test
data.description: Thai League 1 leaders Buriram United will take on Sisaket United in the northeastern derby at Chang Arena today.

data.title: Cheung halfway to historic victory, Jazz tied for third
data.description: HONG KONG: Matthew Cheung has set up a thrilling weekend of golf for Hong Kong's golf fans after taking the halfway lead in the Hong Kong Open as he attempts to become the first player from the territory to win the prestigious title in its 65-year history.

data.title: Orange shadow looms over PP
data.description: The recent warning by former Future Forward Party (FFP) secretary-general Piyabutr Saengkanokkul that the People's Party (PP) should not allow politics to descend into "entertainocracy" is more than a criticism of political communication. It also highlights a lingering reality for the PP: the political shadow of its predecessor remains difficult to escape.

data.title: 2 Chinese Uyghurs pardoned
data.description: Two Chinese Uyghur men detained in Thailand have received royal pardons and are awaiting deportation, a Thai official and an activist said on Thursday, though it was not yet clear where they will go.

data.title: NHRC faults navy over conscript's death
data.description: The National Human Rights Commission has ruled that delays in providing medical treatment to a navy conscript who died during training violated his right to timely healthcare, recommending compensation for his family and reforms to prevent similar cases.

data.title: Ministry offers aid over campus move
data.description: The Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation Ministry has said it will cut tuition fees by 50% and arrange alternative laboratories for students affected by the relocation of Rajamangala University of Technology Tawan-ok's Uthenthawai Campus.

data.title: Lorry driver arrested over suspected waste dumping
data.description: Police have arrested a truck driver and seized an 18-wheel lorry carrying suspected industrial waste allegedly destined for illegal dumping in Sa Kaeo.

data.title: Govt proposes changes to snooker and boxing rules
data.description: The government has opened a month-long public consultation on gambling regulation amendments to ease youth snooker restrictions and modernise boxing competition rules.

data.title: Irish ties set for fresh push
data.description: Chiang Mai is seeking closer ties with Ireland in tourism, agriculture and trade to boost economic and cultural links.

data.title: Passionin motion
data.description: Nostalgia poured thick when Hong Kong's Jumbo Floating Restaurant, an iconic spot that was forced to close due to Covid-19 in 2020 after four decades of operation, appeared on the screen at the Hong Kong Cultural Centre's Studio Theatre in Tsim Sha Tsui. Audiences soon found themselves sailing through a tide of motifs -- neon-lit streets, flats, colonial buildings, churches, vessels and food -- much like the Star Ferry crossing Victoria Harbour, just a stone's throw away. The piano conjured a pleasant daydream, at least until something strange happened.

data.description: Kasetsart University has defended legal protection for four new holy basil, or kaprao, varieties, saying registration does not automatically restrict farmers from growing other varieties.

data.title: Thai coral bacteria set for space mission
data.description: Thai scientists are preparing to send bacteria isolated from Thai corals to the International Space Station (ISS) for the first time, in a pioneering experiment to study how microorganisms adapt to extreme conditions and potentially improve coral reef conservation and restoration.

data.title: Thailand seeks to boost SME exports
data.description: Thailand is seeking to expand export opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by improving access to international markets, financing and digital trade.

data.title: Ekniti backs sin tax changes
data.description: Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has backed a proposal to end earmarked taxes for four organisations and redirect more than 14 billion baht a year to the national budget, saying it is consistent with the State Fiscal and Financial Disciplines Act.

data.title: Speaker of House calls for a deal
data.description: House Speaker Sophon Zarum has urged government and opposition whips to reach a compromise on the schedule for a no-confidence debate, saying the opposition was willing to reduce its demand from five days to four if the debate was held in November or December.

data.title: Saysunee lands gold, Pongsakorn sizzles
data.description: Wheelchair fencer Saysunee Jana finally struck gold at the Asian Para Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026, while wheelchair racer Pongsakorn Paeyo set a Games record for a third straight 400m title, on the penultimate day of competition in Japan on Friday.

data.title: Signs point to renewed major US military ops against Iran
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The United States appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran, but there is unlikely to be a military solution for either side in the devastating conflict, experts say.
